Answer all questions.  For each question there are four possible answers A, B, C and D. Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the multiple choice answer sheet.  Follow the instructions on the multiple choice answer sheet.  Write in soft pencil.  Write your name, centre number and candidate number on the multiple choice answer sheet in the spaces provided unless this has been done for you.  Do not use correction fluid.  Do not write on any bar codes.  You may use a calculator. INFORMATION  The total mark for this paper is 30.  Each correct answer will score one mark.  Any rough working should be done on this question paper.

In a clothing business, after specialisation, real output per worker increased in the first six months but then output per worker began to fall. What might be the most likely reason for the reduction in productivity?

options.A: An increase in output per worker in the long run depends on an increase in pay.
options.B: An increase in output per worker requires more capital.
options.D: Workers get bored if they are repeating the same work.

questions.questionText: A wine producer and bottler wanted to expand its production significantly. To finance the expansion it offered investors discounts on restaurant meals if they bought 2000 shares in the company. Which factors of production are most likely to be involved in this expansion?

options.D: enterprise only

questions.questionText: Which statement is positive?

options.A: All taxes should be proportional to income.
options.B: A progressive tax is a fair tax.
options.C: Greater equality of income is desirable.
options.D: Income inequality is decreasing.

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the change in a country’s production possibility curve from PQ to PR. P public goods O Q R private goods What increases as a result of the change from PQ to PR?

options.C: the opportunity cost of private goods
options.D: the opportunity cost of public goods

A firm produces a good using a very labour-intensive process. There is an increase in the price of the good. Under which conditions will the supply of the firm’s good be most price elastic? nature of the level of labour employed unemployment in by the firm the economy

options.D: unskilled low

questions.questionText: What is most likely to cause the demand curve of an inferior good to shift to the right?

options.D: a rise in the price of a complement

questions.questionText: The diagram shows four supply curves. Which curve has a price elasticity of supply of 1 for all levels of quantity supplied? A C B price D O amount supplied per period
The diagram shows a shift of the supply curve in a market from S to S .
Good X has a substitute, good Y, and a complement, good Z. The price of good Y decreases and the price of good Z increases. Why might the equilibrium price of good X remain unchanged?

options.A: Producers of good X adopt new technology.
options.B: Producers of good X receive a subsidy.
options.C: Some firms stop production of good X.
options.D: The tax on the production of good X is cut.

questions.questionText: In the diagram, S and S are the supply curves for an agricultural product in years 1 and 2
Inequality in an economy can be categorised as either income inequality or wealth inequality. What is most likely to cause greater wealth inequality than income inequality?

options.B: an increase in the value of property
options.C: a reduction in the minimum wage
options.D: a reduction in the rate of interest paid on savings

questions.questionText: A product with infinite elasticity of supply has sales of 1000 units a week at a price of $1 per unit. Price elasticity of demand is 1.5 over the relevant range. The government imposes a tax of 10%. What will be the government’s weekly tax revenue from this product?

The table shows the values of Consumer Prices Index (CPI) and a worker’s salary in 2022 and 2023. CPI 2022 100 CPI 2023 110 worker’s salary 2022 $20000 worker’s salary 2023 $25000 What is the real value of the worker’s salary in 2023 compared with 2022?
An economy experiences rising unemployment due to incomes falling as a result of a virus pandemic. How would this unemployment be classified?

options.D: structural

questions.questionText: What is likely to move an economy’s aggregate demand curve to the right?

options.C: a fall in the exchange rate
options.D: a fall in the government budget deficit

questions.questionText: Which items have to be added to and subtracted from Gross Domestic Product at market prices to calculate the value of Gross Domestic Product at basic prices?

options.A: capital consumption and net property income from abroad
options.C: net property income from abroad and subsidies
options.D: subsidies and expenditure taxes

questions.questionText: In an economy with an interest rate of 4% per annum, the rate of inflation falls from 5% to 3% per annum. What will be a benefit of this fall?

options.A: Menu costs will fall to zero.
options.B: People on fixed incomes will be better off in real terms.
options.C: Savers will gain in real terms.
options.D: The purchasing power of the currency will rise.

questions.questionText: What is an example of a macroeconomic policy?

options.A: encourage the consumption of merit goods
options.B: reduce pollution in the steel industry
options.D: reduce unemployment in the service sector

questions.questionText: Which supply-side policy is likely to lower real output before raising it?

options.A: increased spending on early years education
options.D: subsidies to exporters

questions.questionText: An economy is in equilibrium at point E on the diagram. The government reduces its expenditure on defence. Which point on the diagram shows the new equilibrium? AS AS
The number of people employed in a country and the level of unemployment both decrease. What could explain this?

options.B: an increase in the level of unemployment benefits
options.C: an increase in the age at which state pensions are payable
options.D: an increase in the number of university students

questions.questionText: Which circumstances would most help a firm to gain from a depreciation of the exchange rate?

options.A: It sells mainly abroad and relies on domestic suppliers for inputs.
options.B: It sells mainly abroad and relies on foreign suppliers for inputs.
options.C: It sells mainly in its home market and relies on domestic suppliers for inputs.
options.D: It sells mainly in its home market and relies on foreign suppliers for inputs.

questions.questionText: A country has a floating exchange rate. Its current account on the balance of payments moves from a surplus to a deficit. Which rate is likely to increase in the short run as a consequence of this worsening of its current account?

options.D: unemployment rate

questions.questionText: Which policy is most likely to reduce a balance of payments deficit without causing inflation?

options.D: decreased import tariffs

questions.questionText: The table shows the average price of exports and imports. Which combination of changes in export prices and import prices could result in a country’s terms of trade increasing from 100 to 110? the average price the average price of exports of imports

options.D: rises by 10% remains unchanged

questions.questionText: What is not an example of protectionism?

options.A: the European Union (EU) requiring goods imported into member states to meet safety standards
options.B: the Pakistan government increasing the rate of goods and services tax (GST) on some exported goods from 2% to 5%
options.C: the Nigeria government banning the import of packaged sugar
options.D: the US imposing a 35% tariff on tyres imported from China

questions.questionText: Turkey imported $220 million worth of goods and services. Turkey exported $12 million worth of goods and services during the same period. Its net income was –$15 million. What is Turkey’s current account balance?

options.D: +$247 million
